title: Distinct Extreme Scores in Random Round-Robin Tournaments
summary: We consider a general round-robin tournament model with equally strong players, where $X_{ij}$ denotes the score of player $i$ against player $j$. We assume that $X_{ij}$ takes values in a countable subset of $[0,1]$ and satisfies $X_{ij}+X_{ji}=1$. We prove that if $k(n)\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and $\frac{k(n)^2\sqrt{\log(n/k(n))}}{\sqrt n}\to 0,$ then, with probability tending to one, the largest $k(n)$ scores are all distinct.
